what_worked: Deal-sourcing framework (cheap+growing vs flat) with payback periods is genuinely original and decision-useful.
fix_next: Verify every category median against the raw data — Education, AI, Content Creation, and Marketing medians all diverge from reference values.
verdict: Strong narrative arc and real insights, undermined by multiple incorrect category medians.
factual_error_detail: Slide 4: AI median stated $446 vs ref $503; Education median $2,142 vs ref $2,435; Content Creation median $1,254 vs ref $1,237.50 (minor); Marketing median $1,586 vs ref $2,369.50 (large). Slide 3: Mean MRR ~$13,472 implies total ~$13.47M vs ref $15.60M (denominator unclear — may exclude zero-revenue rows but not stated). Slide 7: B2B 5.7x B2C claim ($1,036/$181=5.7x) is plausible on its own numbers but exec summary says '3–6x' which is vague; the 'per user' framing in exec summary conflates MRR with per-visitor metric. Slide 8: uses averages for growth despite deck's own median-first principle, no caveat given.

evidence.insight: Slides 10-11 build a novel deal-screening framework with payback periods and growth filters; Kickly anomaly flag shows analytical maturity; volume-vs-value divergence on slide 4 is a genuine finding.
evidence.narrative: Four-point thesis on slide 2 maps cleanly to slides 3-11: concentration → category economics → geography → audience → growth → caveats → deal screening. Arc moves from landscape to actionable shortlist.
evidence.framing: Slide 1 states scope/date/sample. Slide 9 dedicates full page to four limitations (selection bias, self-reported, snapshot, missingness). Category missing '27%' stated vs 27.4% ref — close. Audience clearly positioned as investor/acquirer.
evidence.accuracy: Marketing median off by ~$783 (slide 4). AI median off by ~$57. Education median off by ~$293. Mean MRR implies wrong total revenue. Growth slide uses averages contradicting the deck's own median-first principle without caveat. Top-10% = 82% claim cannot be verified against reference (ref gives top-10 share at 49.6%, different metric).
evidence.visual: Consistent dark/red/white palette with clean bar charts and labeled values. Slide 8 has serious label-overlap rendering issues ('Content Cre-60.0%' and '-450.0%any' illegible). Table on slide 11 well-structured. Overall functional but slide 8 legibility problem lowers score.
evidence.ai_slop: none — language is dataset-specific throughout, caveats are genuine, no generic filler or decorative graphics

change_reason: Lowered visual from 7.0 to 6.5 due to slide 8 label-overlap rendering issues making two data points illegible; all other scores confirmed after independent review.
